messages.subject: Facet_grid and Pie Charts
parts:
Hello all,

I am not able to reproduce Fig 2.4 in Leland Wilkinson's Grammar of
Graphics book (p. 38). I know that there is a tutorial on this example
here:

http://www.r-bloggers.com/pie-charts-in-ggplot2/

However, I'm wondering whether I can create this plot directly from
the original data source, making all the necessary transformations and
summary statistics with ggplot2.

Here what I wrote so far (and does not yield the correct output):

library(ggplot2)
n <- 3835; n.males <- floor(n*.74); n.females <- n-n.males
answers <- c("Rarely", "Infrequently", "Occasionally", "Frequently",
"Not Sure")
resp.males <-
sample(answers,n.males,replace=TRUE,prob=c(0.3,0.15,0.1,0.07,0.38))
resp.females <-
sample(answers,n.females,replace=TRUE,prob=c(0.08,0.11,0.17,0.32,0.32))
acls <- data.frame(Response=factor(c(resp.males,resp.females)),
Gender=factor(rep(c('Males','Females'), c(n.males,n.females))))

pie <- ggplot(data=acls, aes(x = factor(1), fill=Response))

pie <- pie + geom_bar(width = 1, stat = "bin")
pie <- pie + facet_grid(.~Gender)
pie <- pie + coord_polar(theta = "y")

Any hints?

Thanks,

Adrian

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Facet_grid and Pie Charts
parts:
Hi Adrian,

It looks like there's a bit of a bug with polar coordinates at the
moment, but in principle, I think you want: facet_grid(.~Gender,
scales = "free_y")

Hadley
